text: And the most important geographical fact, which most people are not aware of, the narrowest point in the Strait of Hormuz is 21 nautical miles.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And this is of profound importance to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, to the Member's specific question, yes, I have engaged with the Iranian Foreign Minister before the war.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Because to do so would be implicitly eroding this legal principle.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, again, this is another example of Singapore upholding principle, not taking sides.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The larger geostrategic backdrop to this is, whether we realise it or not, the world has become more violent and more volatile, and there is a price to be paid for that.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Second, what the Strait of Hormuz has shown is that even in this digital age, chokepoints and physical delivery still matter.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And the third point which we need to register in Singapore is that it is not enough to be an oasis of safety, security, cohesion, wealth and even having the military ability to protect ourselves – because if our region is aflame and with war and missiles flying, no oasis can be safe.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The upshot of these three observations is that there is an insurance premium to be paid.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, let us be upfront with our people, explain the dangers, no sugar-coating, explain what needs to be done, including paying that insurance premium.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We need to alert our people, but not be alarmist.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we have to walk that fine tight rope.

text: I cannot possibly cover every perceivable permutation or conceivable combination that can come up.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have taken it upon ourselves to make sure that we have provided contingencies for different scenarios – from single geographical chokepoints to multiple geographical chokepoints.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think for us, we have done every possible measure.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have taken it upon ourselves to open up every single diversification measure possible and available to us today.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To the Member's point on what if these countries decide to curtail back the gas supply?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Of course, how long can we survive if everything is taken away, I think that is something that I cannot share with you.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And everyone here would understand why I am not at liberty to share this with you.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that the House can appreciate the very delicate balance we are all in today and how we should all be working closely together as one united nation.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
text: But in view of time, I will send the question in bucket two to Minister of State Jeffrey.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
text: My question in the third bucket is regarding what Minister Vivian has just mentioned.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
text: The Strait of Hormuz is undeniably important to Singapore and the wider region due to its role in the global energy flow.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
text: I believe the Strait of Malacca is even more critical to us, as one of the world's busiest shipping lanes and a key artery for trade, any disruption there would have immediate and far-reaching consequences for Singapore's economics and supply chains.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
text: This raises an important question for all of us.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
text: Has our Government fully internalise the lesson from potential vulnerability in such strategic chokepoints?

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
text: In particular, are we sufficiently prepared for a scenario where the Strait of Malacca is disrupted, whether through geopolitical tension, blockages or other crises?

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
text: And do we have robust contingency plans to mitigate the impact?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: With that, we have had almost three-and-a-half hours of debate on the Ministerial Statements.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think all clarifications have been sought and answered, sometimes more than once.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 5.30 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 5.11 pm until 5.30 pm.
